item: The erase rewrites a plaintext main database in full after unlinking it and says the crypto-erase guarantee only for an encrypted one
summary: A main database known to be plaintext (head-only before: its body stayed on the disk), in the data folder or where DATABASE_URL keeps it, is checked against its identity read before anything is opened (lstat; gone, unidentifiable, a link or another file: never touched), each of its files opened no-follow through its folder handle and kept, page 1 / the log / the log index head destroyed through the handle at once (R818), unlinked at once, and at the very end of the erase, only after the app's own pool on it is disposed (else first page only, the rest said as not overwritten; R818), rewritten in full through the kept handles over every data region (SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE, else the logical size with the 64 MiB reserve; R797) after a fstat check, fsynced, the handles closed by the late pass after the pool (R789). Windows falls back to the first page then the unlink. Reported apart from Wiped n/n (report plaintext_store: overwritten, partially overwritten, not overwritten or first page, the reason, deleted, other names by count). _LIMIT_NOTE, the held-store note and the free-space overwrite's note claim the guarantee only for a main database known to be encrypted; plaintext and unknown fail closed with their own sentences (CLI, HTTP, panic page; strings x12). No deadline: a notice that it may take minutes (CLI, page), a stop partway said as partially overwritten; other names said to lead to the overwritten content (R818). Hard-link witness tests in both locations; a stop before the body rewrite finds page 1 and the log destroyed; a pool not confirmed closed and on the HTTP path; a stop mid-rewrite; a link swapped in at the path.
